label: Clinical metagenomics (urine and ascites)
description: Curated pathogen tiers for urine and ascites, commensal flora, skin-associated bacteria and likely artifacts. Ported from the INDIVO Explorer curation seed; entries carry notes and literature references. Tiers follow the BILULU urine traffic light and the SBP literature for ascites.

lists.label: Urine · typically uropathogenic
lists.help: BILULU red tier: considered the causative agent of a symptomatic UTI  essentially regardless of colony count.

entries.name: Acinetobacter baumannii
entries.note: Major multidrug-resistant Gram-negative cause of catheter-associated and complicated/nosocomial UTI; roughly 1 in 5 A. baumannii clinical isolates come from urinary sites and several centers report it among the most comm…
refs: {"title": "Urinary tract colonization is enhanced by a plasmid that regulates uropathogenic Acinetobacter baumannii chromosomal genes", "url": "https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-10706-y", "year": 2019}

entries.name: Aerococcus urinae
entries.note: Valid species (LPSN 1992). Recognized fastidious Gram-positive uropathogen; causes cystitis, pyelonephritis, urosepsis, endocarditis. Causative in symptomatic pure/predominant growth. Verified confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Aerococcus urinae: an emerging gram-positive pathogen causing urinary tract infection", "url": "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8380466/", "year": 2021}

entries.name: Citrobacter freundii
entries.note: Valid Enterobacterales uropathogen (BILULU RED tier). Causative in complicated/nosocomial UTI; catheter/instrumentation-linked, often ESBL/AmpC. Verified confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Citrobacter: An emerging health care associated urinary pathogen", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3836000/", "year": 2013}

entries.name: Corynebacterium urealyticum
entries.note: Valid name (Pitcher 1992, former CDC group D-2). Urease-positive uropathogen causing alkaline-encrusted cystitis/pyelitis with struvite; verified RED tier confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Encrusted Uropathy: A Comprehensive Overview\u2014To the Bottom of the Crust", "url": "https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2020.609024/full", "year": 2020}

entries.name: Enterobacter cloacae
entries.note: Valid name; Enterobacterales, classical biofilm-forming uropathogen causing complicated/HCA-UTI, pyelonephritis, urosepsis. RED/definite tier confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Laboratory diagnosis of urinary tract infections: Towards a BILULU consensus guideline", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29427686/", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Escherichia coli
entries.note: Canonical uropathogen: >80% of uncomplicated UTIs; treated as causative regardless of colony count in symptomatic patients. Valid nomenclature. RED/verified tier.
refs: {"title": "European Association of Urology Guidelines on Urological Infections: Summary of the 2024 Guidelines", "url": "https://www.europeanurology.com/article/S0302-2838(24)02263-2/fulltext", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Klebsiella aerogenes
entries.note: Reclassified from Enterobacter aerogenes; a common opportunistic, frequently ESBL/AmpC-producing nosocomial Enterobacterales uropathogen causing complicated/recurrent UTI, pyelonephritis and urosepsis.
refs: {"title": "Case report: A successfully treated case of community-acquired urinary tract infection due to Klebsiella aerogenes in Bangladesh", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10330784/", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Klebsiella oxytoca
entries.note: Valid name (Flugge 1886). Klebsiella/Enterobacterales = primary Gram-neg uropathogen, BILULU RED tier; 2nd most common Klebsiella in UTI after K. pneumoniae. Verified confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Klebsiella oxytoca: An emerging pathogen?", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5192185/", "year": 2017}

entries.name: Klebsiella pneumoniae
entries.note: K. pneumoniae (valid nomenclature) is a primary Enterobacterales uropathogen, 2nd to E. coli; always-significant RED-tier per BILULU/EAU. Verified confirmed.
refs: {"title": "European Association of Urology Guidelines on Urological Infections: Summary of the 2024 Guidelines", "url": "https://www.europeanurology.com/article/S0302-2838(24)02263-2/fulltext", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Proteus mirabilis
entries.note: Valid name; classic urease-producing Enterobacterales uropathogen, major cause of complicated/catheter-assoc UTI and struvite stones. Verified (RED tier) confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Proteus mirabilis and Urinary Tract Infections", "url": "https://journals.asm.org/doi/10.1128/microbiolspec.uti-0017-2013", "year": 2015}

entries.name: Providencia stuartii
entries.note: Confirmed: P. stuartii (valid, family Morganellaceae/Proteeae) is a recognized uropathogen, esp. catheter-associated UTI w/ biofilm. RED/verified tier.
refs: {"title": "Transposon Insertion Site Sequencing of Providencia stuartii: Essential Genes, Fitness Factors for Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infection, and the Impact of Polymicrobial Infection on Fitness Requirements", "url": "https://journals.asm.org/doi/10.1128/msphere.00412-20", "year": 2020}

entries.name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
entries.note: Established uropathogen; ESKAPE non-fermenter, ~10% of CAUTI and key complicated-UTI agent per EAU/BILULU. Valid nomenclature. Verified tier correct.
refs: {"title": "Urinary tract infections and catheter-associated urinary tract infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa", "url": "https://journals.asm.org/doi/10.1128/mmbr.00066-22", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Serratia marcescens
entries.note: Valid Enterobacterales (Yersiniaceae) name; classic healthcare/catheter-associated uropathogen causing complicated UTI, pyelonephritis, urosepsis. Verified tier confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Serratia marcescens: A Versatile Opportunistic Pathogen with Emerging Clinical and Biotechnological Significance", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12691863/", "year": 2025}

entries.name: Staphylococcus aureus
entries.note: S. aureus is a recognized uropathogen treated regardless of colony count in true UTI; in urine also flags possible haematogenous seeding/bacteremia. Valid nomenclature. Verified.
refs: {"title": "Bacterial Urinary Tract Infection (UTI) Treatment Guidelines (Johns Hopkins Antimicrobial Stewardship)", "url": "https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/-/media/antimicrobial-stewardship/bacterial_uti_guidelines.pdf", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Staphylococcus saprophyticus
entries.note: Valid name. 2nd most common cause of uncomplicated cystitis in young women; the one CoNS treated as a true uropathogen at any colony count. RED/verified confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Staphylococcus saprophyticus Infection - StatPearls - NCBI Bookshelf", "url": "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK482367/", "year": 2023}

lists.label: Urine · potentially uropathogenic
lists.help: BILULU yellow tier: significant only above threshold counts, in  pure/predominant growth, or in specific hosts (catheter, pregnancy,  immunocompromise).

entries.name: Actinotignum schaalii
entries.note: Valid name (formerly Actinobaculum schaalii). Genuine but fastidious uropathogen; also urobiome member. Significant in elderly/urologic-abnormality hosts and pure/predominant growth = YELLOW, not RED.
refs: {"title": "Actinotignum schaalii (formerly Actinobaculum schaalii): a newly recognized pathogen\u2014review of the literature", "url": "https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1198743X15009799", "year": 2016}

entries.name: Aerococcus sanguinicola
entries.note: Valid sp. (Lawson 2001). BILULU-listed uropathogen but emerging/opportunistic: significant in elderly men w/ UT abnormalities or catheters. YELLOW, not RED.
refs: {"title": "Bacteremia with Aerococcus sanguinicola: Case Series with Characterization of Virulence Properties", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4324188/", "year": 2014}

entries.name: Aerococcus viridans
entries.note: Valid name; type species, often confused w/ A. sanguinicola. Rare uropathogen of uncertain significance, only in predominant growth/elderly/post-surgical hosts. YELLOW.
refs: {"title": "Aerococcus Viridans: A Rare Pathogen Causing Urinary Tract Infection", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5324413/", "year": 2017}

entries.name: Candida albicans
entries.note: Demote verified→potential. Candiduria is usually colonization; significant only in catheter/diabetes/immunocompromised/ICU hosts. IDSA does not treat asymptomatic candiduria. YELLOW, not RED.
refs: {"title": "Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Candidiasis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4725385/", "year": 2016}

entries.name: Candida parapsilosis
entries.note: Valid name. Candiduria usually colonization (catheter/biofilm); pathogenic only in symptomatic or high-risk hosts (catheter, ICU, immunocompromised). YELLOW/potential confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Microbiological Relevance of Candida in Urine Cultures", "url": "https://www.mdpi.com/2309-608X/11/7/483", "year": 2025}

entries.name: Candida tropicalis
entries.note: Valid name; 3rd most common urinary Candida (~10%). Usually asymptomatic colonization; significance threshold/host-dependent (catheter, ICU, immunocompromise). YELLOW/potential.
refs: {"title": "Microbiological Relevance of Candida in Urine Cultures", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12298255/", "year": 2025}

entries.name: Citrobacter koseri
entries.note: Opportunistic Enterobacterales uropathogen (the list already verifies the sibling C. freundii). Causes healthcare-associated UTI, particularly with catheterization/instrumentation and in immunocompromised/elderly hosts;…
refs: {"title": "Citrobacter: An emerging health care associated urinary pathogen", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3836000/", "year": 2013}

entries.name: Corynebacterium amycolatum
entries.note: Valid name (Collins 1988). Skin commensal & frequent urine contaminant; opportunistic uropathogen in pure growth/catheter/immunocompromised. YELLOW, not RED C. urealyticum.
refs: {"title": "Draft genome sequences of four Corynebacterium amycolatum strains isolated from female urine samples", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11384733/", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Corynebacterium striatum
entries.note: Valid name. Skin/coryneform flora, frequent urine contaminant, but emerging MDR opportunist; uropathogenic in pure growth in catheter/immunocompromised hosts = YELLOW.
refs: {"title": "Clinical Characteristics and Risk Factors of Corynebacterium striatum Infection in Normally Sterile Body Fluids and Urine Specimens", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12747092/", "year": 2025}

entries.name: Enterobacter hormaechei
entries.note: Now recognized as the predominant species within the Enterobacter cloacae complex in clinical isolates; an ESBL/carbapenemase-prone nosocomial Enterobacterales uropathogen documented in catheter-associated UTI.
refs: {"title": "Draft genome sequences of an Enterobacter hormaechei and Providencia rettgeri isolated from the urine of a male experiencing a catheter-associated urinary tract infection", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11385441/", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Enterococcus faecalis
entries.note: Valid name; recognized enterococcal uropathogen but significance is count/host-dependent (catheter, complicated, predominant growth) = YELLOW/potential, not unconditional RED.
refs: {"title": "Laboratory diagnosis of urinary tract infections: Towards a BILULU consensus guideline", "url": "https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0167701218300940", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Enterococcus faecium
entries.note: Valid name (Schleifer & Kilpper-Balz 1984). Conditional uropathogen: significant at high count/predominant growth, catheter/HAI/immunocompromised; often colonizer in mixed flora. YELLOW.
refs: {"title": "Enterococcal Urinary Tract Infections: A Review of the Pathogenicity, Epidemiology, and Treatment", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10135011/", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Gardnerella vaginalis
entries.note: Valid name (G. vaginalis, type sp. post-2019 split). Urobiome/vaginal flora; conditionally significant in recurrent UTI, dysbiosis, E. coli reactivation. YELLOW, not RED.
refs: {"title": "Gardnerella vaginalis in Recurrent Urinary Tract Infection Is Associated with Dysbiosis of the Bladder Microbiome", "url": "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9100223/", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Morganella morganii
entries.note: Valid Proteeae sp.; opportunistic uropathogen of complicated/catheter-assoc UTI, significant in specific hosts/threshold growth, not obligate. Demote verified->potential (YELLOW).
refs: {"title": "Comparative Genome Analysis of Uropathogenic Morganella morganii Strains", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558430/", "year": 2019}

entries.name: Nakaseomyces glabratus
entries.note: Valid current name (formerly C. glabrata). 2nd most common urinary yeast; candiduria usually asymptomatic colonization, significant only in catheter/ICU/immunocompromised hosts. YELLOW/potential.
refs: {"title": "Characteristics and Clinical Relevance of Candiduria in Hospitalized Patients", "url": "https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0383/15/5/1881", "year": 2026}

entries.name: Pichia kudriavzevii
entries.note: Teleomorph/current name for Candida krusei; a recognized cause of funguria/candiduria in catheterized, diabetic and broadly antibiotic-exposed hosts, clinically important for its intrinsic fluconazole resistance (require…
refs: {"title": "Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Candidiasis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America", "url": "https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/candidiasis/", "year": 2016}

entries.name: Proteus vulgaris
entries.note: Urease-positive Proteus species causing UTI and struvite (magnesium ammonium phosphate) stone formation via urea hydrolysis and urine alkalinization, similar mechanism to the verified P. mirabilis. Less common than P.
refs: {"title": "Proteus Infections: Background, Etiology, Pathophysiology", "url": "https://emedicine.medscape.com/article/226434-overview"}

entries.name: Providencia rettgeri
entries.note: Urease-positive, biofilm-forming Enterobacterales closely associated with long-term catheter-associated UTI and crystalline catheter encrustation; increasingly reported as MDR/pan-drug-resistant.
refs: {"title": "Uropathogenic Pan-Drug-Resistant Providencia rettgeri Infection in a Patient With an Indwelling Urinary Catheter: A Case Report", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11628197/", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Schaalia turicensis
entries.note: Fastidious Gram-positive anaerobe/microaerophile in the same emerging-uropathogen group as Actinotignum schaalii (already listed); reported in UTI and urogenital infections, easily missed on standard aerobic culture and…
refs: {"title": "Beyond the usual suspects: emerging uropathogens in the microbiome age", "url": "https://doi.org/10.3389/fruro.2023.1212590", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Staphylococcus epidermidis
entries.note: Valid CoNS (non-saprophyticus). In voided urine usually skin/periurethral contamination, but conditional uropathogen in catheter/instrumented/immunocompromised hosts at significant pure growth. Tier: potential.
refs: {"title": "Significance of Coagulase-Negative Staphylococcus in Urine", "url": "https://academic.oup.com/jid/article-abstract/127/2/179/878548", "year": 1973}

entries.name: Staphylococcus haemolyticus
entries.note: CoNS, valid name. Usually skin/periurethral contaminant in voided urine, but emerging MDR conditional uropathogen significant in pure/predominant growth, catheter/nosocomial hosts (YELLOW).
refs: {"title": "Staphylococcus haemolyticus as an emerging infectious agent in female genital and urinary tract: a narrative review", "url": "https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44337-026-00575-y", "year": 2026}

entries.name: Staphylococcus warneri
entries.note: CoNS skin commensal, usually voided-urine contaminant; rare uropathogen only in pure/significant growth or compromised/catheterised hosts. YELLOW tier.
refs: {"title": "Staphylococcus warneri: Skin Commensal and a Rare Cause of Urinary Tract Infection", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7263002/", "year": 2020}

entries.name: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia
entries.note: Intrinsically multidrug-resistant non-fermenting Gram-negative; an emerging cause of complicated/catheter-associated UTI that tends to follow a severe clinical course in patients with urological disease or immunosuppress…
refs: {"title": "Stenotrophomonas Maltophilia and Urinary Tract Infections: A Systematic Review", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9304920/", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Streptococcus agalactiae
entries.note: S. agalactiae (GBS) is host/threshold-dependent in urine: significant in pregnancy & at high counts, often asymptomatic colonization otherwise. Potential (YELLOW), not verified.
refs: {"title": "Laboratory diagnosis of urinary tract infections: Towards a BILULU consensus guideline", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29427686/", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Streptococcus anginosus
entries.note: Valid name. SAG/anginosus group = normal oral-GI flora, emerging conditional uropathogen: enriched in urgency incontinence, significant in immunocompromise/predominant growth. YELLOW/potential, not verified.
refs: {"title": "Beyond the usual suspects: emerging uropathogens in the microbiome age", "url": "https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/urology/articles/10.3389/fruro.2023.1212590/full", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Streptococcus dysgalactiae
entries.note: Beta-hemolytic group C/G streptococcus reported as a uropathogen and cause of bacteriuria/UTI, paralleling the group A (S. pyogenes) and group B (S. agalactiae) streptococci already in the lists.

entries.name: Streptococcus pyogenes
entries.note: Valid name. GAS is an uncommon, conditional uropathogen: genuine UTI/urethritis in pure/predominant growth or complicated hosts, often perineal contamination otherwise. YELLOW/potential confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Streptococcus pyogenes: An Unusual Cause of Urethritis", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11470757/", "year": 2024}

entries.name: [Candida] auris
entries.note: Emerging multidrug-resistant nosocomial yeast increasingly reported as the etiologic agent of UTI/candiduria, frequently fluconazole-resistant; first-line treatment is echinocandin or liposomal amphotericin B.
refs: {"title": "Candida auris Urinary Tract Infections and Possible Treatment", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7764735/", "year": 2020}

entries.name: Alloscardovia omnicolens
entries.note: Valid name (Alloscardovia, est. 2007). Emerging opportunistic uropathogen; significant mainly in pure/predominant growth or compromised/elderly hosts. YELLOW/potential, not RED.
refs: {"title": "Beyond the usual suspects: emerging uropathogens in the microbiome age", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12327349/", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Mycoplasma hominis
entries.note: Urogenital mollicute with an etiologic role in acute urethral syndrome and upper urinary tract infection in selected hosts; missed by routine culture.
refs: {"title": "A Systematic Review of Mycoplasma and Ureaplasma in Urogynaecology", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5734936/", "year": 2017}

entries.name: Ureaplasma urealyticum
entries.note: Cell-wall-deficient urogenital organism; urease-positive and implicated in nongonococcal urethritis, acute urethral syndrome and possibly infection-related struvite stones.
refs: {"title": "A Systematic Review of Mycoplasma and Ureaplasma in Urogynaecology", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5734936/", "year": 2017}

lists.label: Urine · urogenital mucosal flora
lists.help: BILULU green tier: normal urogenital / periurethral commensals (incl.  vaginal & skin flora); in voided urine usually contamination.

entries.name: Aerococcus christensenii
entries.note: Validly named (1999) vaginal commensal; rarely if ever a true uropathogen. In voided urine usually genital-flora contamination, unlike A. urinae/sanguinicola. Demote to GREEN.
refs: {"title": "Aerococcus christensenii sp. nov., from the human vagina", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10425770/", "year": 1999}

entries.name: Anaerococcus prevotii
entries.note: Valid name (type species of Anaerococcus). GPAC commensal of skin/urogenital tract & urobiome; in voided urine = mucosal contamination. GREEN/flora_commensal.
refs: {"title": "Gram-positive anaerobic cocci \u2013 commensals and opportunistic pathogens", "url": "https://academic.oup.com/femsre/article/37/4/520/2399123", "year": 2013}

entries.name: Bifidobacterium breve
entries.note: Valid name (ATCC 15700). Gut/urogenital commensal; in voided urine reflects flora/contamination. UTI case reports are B. scardovii, not B. breve. GREEN tier.
refs: {"title": "Gram-Positive Uropathogens, Polymicrobial Urinary Tract Infection, and the Emerging Microbiota of the Urinary Tract", "url": "https://journals.asm.org/doi/10.1128/microbiolspec.uti-0012-2012", "year": 2016}

entries.name: Corynebacterium tuberculostearicum
entries.note: Valid name (Feurer 2004). Lipophilic skin commensal; in voided urine usually contamination, UTI only at case-report rarity. Per BILULU only C. urealyticum is uropathogenic. GREEN/flora.
refs: {"title": "Unveiling a Rarity: First Instance of Urinary Tract Infection Caused by Corynebacterium tuberculostearicum in India", "url": "https://karger.com/cnd/article/14/1/185/916873/Unveiling-a-Rarity-First-Instance-of-Urinary-Tract", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Cutibacterium acnes
entries.note: Skin/genitourinary commensal (ex-Propionibacterium acnes); in voided urine = periurethral/skin contamination, enriched in no-growth samples. GREEN/flora_commensal confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Prostate and urinary microbiomes in prostate cancer development: focus on Cutibacterium acnes", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12133773/", "year": 2025}

entries.name: Fannyhessea vaginae
entries.note: Valid name (ex-Atopobium vaginae). Gram+ anaerobic vaginal/urogenital flora; in voided urine usually contamination, only context-dependent pathogenicity. GREEN.
refs: {"title": "Polymicrobial urine cultures: reconciling contamination with the urobiome while recognizing the pathogens", "url": "https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cellular-and-infection-microbiology/articles/10.3389/fcimb.2025.1562687/full", "year": 2025}

entries.name: Finegoldia magna
entries.note: Valid name (was Peptostreptococcus magnus). Normal GU/skin/urobiome anaerobe; in voided urine usually periurethral flora/contamination, only occasionally pathogenic. GREEN tier confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Finegoldia magna, an Anaerobic Gram-Positive Bacterium of the Normal Human Microbiota, Induces Inflammation by Activating Neutrophils", "url": "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7025542/", "year": 2020}

entries.name: Lactobacillus crispatus
entries.note: Valid name (retained genus, Zheng 2020). Hallmark health-associated urogenital Lactobacillus; in voided urine = vaginal-flora contamination/protective commensal, not a uropathogen. GREEN tier confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Lactobacillus crispatus Limits Bladder Uropathogenic E. coli Infection by Triggering a Host Type I Interferon Response", "url": "https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2117904119", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Lactobacillus gasseri
entries.note: Valid name (L. delbrueckii group, retained genus post-2020). Urogenital/urobiome commensal; in voided urine = vaginal flora; not a uropathogen. GREEN/flora_commensal.
refs: {"title": "Commensal Urinary Lactobacilli Inhibit Major Uropathogens In Vitro With Heterogeneity at Species and Strain Level", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9260849/", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Lactobacillus iners
entries.note: Valid name (Falsen 1999, not renamed in 2020 split). Health-associated urogenital/vaginal Lactobacillus; in voided urine a recognised commensal/contaminant, not uropathogenic. GREEN tier.
refs: {"title": "Commensal Urinary Lactobacilli Inhibit Major Uropathogens In Vitro With Heterogeneity at Species and Strain Level", "url": "https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cellular-and-infection-microbiology/articles/10.3389/fcimb.2022.870603/full", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Lactobacillus jensenii
entries.note: Health-associated vaginal/urogenital commensal; valid name retained post-2020 reclassification. In voided urine = contamination, not uropathogen. GREEN tier.
refs: {"title": "Laboratory diagnosis of urinary tract infections: Towards a BILULU consensus guideline", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29427686/", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Lactobacillus johnsonii
entries.note: Vaginal/urogenital Lactobacillus species forming part of the healthy, Lactobacillus-dominated female urobiome described in core-urinary-microbiota studies; in voided urine represents commensal/contaminant flora rather th…
refs: {"title": "Pre- and postmenopausal women have different core urinary microbiota", "url": "https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-81790-8", "year": 2021}

entries.name: Micrococcus luteus
entries.note: Validated species (Schroeter 1872); ubiquitous skin/periurethral commensal classed as dermal contaminant in voided urine. Not a uropathogen; only opportunistic via bloodstream in immunocompromised hosts. GREEN tier.
refs: {"title": "Laboratory diagnosis of urinary tract infections: Towards a BILULU consensus guideline", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29427686/", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Peptoniphilus harei
entries.note: Valid name (Ezaki 2001). GPAC of urogenital/skin commensal flora; in voided urine = anaerobic microbiome/contaminant, only opportunistic in polymicrobial infections. Not a BILULU uropathogen. GREEN.
refs: {"title": "Gram-positive anaerobic cocci - commensals and opportunistic pathogens", "url": "https://academic.oup.com/femsre/article/37/4/520/2399123", "year": 2013}

entries.name: Prevotella bivia
entries.note: Valid name (LPSN). Gram-neg anaerobe of vaginal/urogenital flora; in voided urine usually contamination, not a recognized uropathogen. GREEN/commensal tier confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Laboratory diagnosis of urinary tract infections: Towards a BILULU consensus guideline", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29427686/", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Staphylococcus capitis
entries.note: Valid species (LPSN). Skin-flora CoNS; in voided urine usually contaminant (GREEN). Significant only in pure high-count growth or catheter/compromised host. Not S. saprophyticus/lugdunensis.
refs: {"title": "Coagulase-negative Staphylococci: a rare cause of urinary tract infections in children with consequences on clinical practice", "url": "https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00431-021-04308-4", "year": 2021}

entries.name: Staphylococcus hominis
entries.note: Valid name (LPSN). CoNS (non-saprophyticus) skin/periurethral flora; in BILULU/EAU usually voided-urine contaminant. Only rarely significant in pure growth/catheter/immunocompromised.
refs: {"title": "Laboratory diagnosis of urinary tract infections: Towards a BILULU consensus guideline", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29427686/", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Streptococcus gordonii
entries.note: Validly named viridans-group oral/mucosal commensal (Kilian 1989). In voided urine it represents commensal/contaminant flora, only rarely a true uropathogen. GREEN tier confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Taxonomic Study of Viridans Streptococci: Description of Streptococcus gordonii sp. nov...", "url": "https://www.microbiologyresearch.org/content/journal/ijsem/10.1099/00207713-39-4-471", "year": 1989}

entries.name: Streptococcus mitis
entries.note: S. mitis (valid; oral/genitourinary viridans commensal) is a typical voided-urine contaminant; true UTI is rare and host-dependent. GREEN flora_commensal.
refs: {"title": "Genomic relatedness and clinical significance of Streptococcus mitis strains isolated from the urogenital tract of sexual partners", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8190612/", "year": 2021}

entries.name: Streptococcus oralis
entries.note: Mitis-group oral/urogenital commensal (valid name, LPSN). In voided urine usually contamination; rarely a true uropathogen in immunocompromised/complicated UTI. Best fit GREEN/flora_commensal.
refs: {"title": "Laboratory diagnosis of urinary tract infections: Towards a BILULU consensus guideline", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29427686/", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Streptococcus salivarius
entries.note: Valid name (LPSN). Oral/periurethral viridans streptococcus; voided-urine contaminant (BILULU GREEN). Pathogenicity only in rare case reports; demote to flora_commensal.
refs: {"title": "Laboratory diagnosis of urinary tract infections: Towards a BILULU consensus guideline", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29427686/", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Streptococcus sanguinis
entries.note: Viridans-group oral/urogenital commensal (BILULU GREEN); in voided urine almost always contamination. Name valid (corrig. of S. sanguis). True UTI rare, needs obstruction/pure growth.
refs: {"title": "Laboratory diagnosis of urinary tract infections: Towards a BILULU consensus guideline", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29427686/", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Prevotella timonensis
entries.note: Anaerobic Gram-negative rod and a recognized member of the urogenital/vaginal-derived urinary microbiome (urobiome), alongside Prevotella bivia which is already in the flora list.
refs: {"title": "Pre- and postmenopausal women have different core urinary microbiota", "url": "https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-81790-8", "year": 2021}

lists.label: Ascites · established SBP pathogen
lists.help: Organisms most frequently cultured from spontaneous bacterial peritonitis  (SBP) / ascitic-fluid infection in cirrhosis.

entries.name: Clostridium perfringens
entries.note: An anaerobic Gram-positive bacillus associated with gut perforation and secondary bacterial peritonitis; a classic anaerobe whose presence in ascitic fluid points to a surgically treatable intra-abdominal source rather t…

entries.name: Enterococcus faecalis
entries.note: Valid nomenclature. Enterococci (incl. E. faecalis) named among commonly cultured SBP organisms; skews to healthcare-associated SBP. Verified per tier def.
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis in Cirrhotic Patients: A Shift in the Microbial Pattern? A Retrospective Analysis", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9274822/", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Escherichia coli
entries.note: E. coli is the single most frequently cultured organism in community-acquired SBP (~50-66% of culture-positive episodes); prototypical translocating enteric GNB. Verified.
refs: {"title": "Recognition of Antibiotic Resistance in Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis Caused by Escherichia coli in Liver Cirrhotic Patients in Civil Hospital Karachi", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6764645/", "year": 2019}

entries.name: Klebsiella pneumoniae
entries.note: Valid name; 2nd most common Enterobacterales SBP agent after E. coli (~12-14% of ascitic-fluid isolates). Classic gut-translocation pathogen of community-acquired SBP. Verified.
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis in Cirrhotic Patients: A Shift in the Microbial Pattern? A Retrospective Analysis", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9274822/", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Listeria monocytogenes
entries.note: Well-documented cause of SBP in cirrhotics and a clinically critical omission: it is intrinsically resistant to the third-generation cephalosporins (cefotaxime/ceftriaxone) used as empiric SBP therapy, so missing it has…
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis Caused by Listeria monocytogenes Associated with Ascitic Fluid Lymphocytosis: A Case Report and Review of Current Empiric Therapy", "url": "https://doi.org/10.1155/2013/832457", "year": 2013}

entries.name: Streptococcus agalactiae
entries.note: Valid name (GBS). Nonenterococcal streptococci are core community-acquired SBP agents; S. agalactiae documented among SBP ascitic-fluid isolates. Verified.
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis in Cirrhotic Patients: A Shift in the Microbial Pattern? A Retrospective Analysis", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9274822/", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Streptococcus anginosus
entries.note: Valid name; anginosus(milleri)-group viridans streptococcus. Streptococci are a verified SBP agent; VGS ~74% of strep SBP isolates, abscess-prone. Less-classic, so medium.
refs: {"title": "Viridans group streptococci: an underestimated cause of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in cirrhotic patients with ascites", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16093870/", "year": 2005}

entries.name: Streptococcus gallolyticus
entries.note: Valid name (S. bovis biotype I, SBSEC group D). Gut-derived streptococcus; documented SBP case series. Streptococci are classic community-acquired SBP agents. Verified.
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis caused by Streptococcus bovis: case series and review of the literature", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12094869/", "year": 2002}

entries.name: Streptococcus mitis
entries.note: Valid name; viridans-group streptococcus. Streptococci are a named verified SBP agent; VGS dominant in SBP series, explicitly not dismissable as contaminant. Verified, not commensal.
refs: {"title": "Viridans group streptococci: an underestimated cause of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in cirrhotic patients with ascites", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16093870/", "year": 2005}

entries.name: Streptococcus parasanguinis
entries.note: Valid name (sanguinis-group VGS). VGS are a documented, underestimated SBP cause in cirrhosis; S. parasanguinis cultured from ascites in SBP. Streptococci are verified-tier.
refs: {"title": "Viridans group streptococci: an underestimated cause of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in cirrhotic patients with ascites", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16093870/", "year": 2005}

entries.name: Streptococcus pneumoniae
entries.note: Established non-enteric streptococcal SBP agent; ~3-6% of culture-proven SBP (not 18-19%, that figure is inflated). Valid nomenclature. Verified holds.
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis: recent guidelines and beyond", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22147550/", "year": 2012}

entries.name: Streptococcus salivarius
entries.note: Valid name. Streptococci are frequent SBP agents; S. salivarius (viridans group) documented in case reports and series as a real SBP cause. Verified.
refs: {"title": "Viridans group streptococci: an underestimated cause of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in cirrhotic patients with ascites", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16093870/", "year": 2005}

entries.name: Streptococcus sanguinis
entries.note: Viridans streptococci (incl. S. sanguinis, valid name) are a frequent, underestimated SBP cause; verified tier lists streptococci. Demote from flora_commensal.
refs: {"title": "Viridans group streptococci: an underestimated cause of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in cirrhotic patients with ascites", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16093870/", "year": 2005}

lists.label: Ascites · potential / opportunistic
lists.help: Cause ascitic-fluid infection in specific settings: healthcare-associated  / nosocomial SBP, secondary bacterial peritonitis, fungal peritonitis,  immunocompromise.

entries.name: Acinetobacter baumannii
entries.note: Nosocomial/HCA-SBP opportunist; MDR non-fermenter cultured from ascitic fluid in cirrhosis, outside community-acquired SBP spectrum. Valid nomenclature.
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis: Etiology, Microbiology, and Clinical Outcomes in Cirrhosis Patients", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11781897/", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Aerococcus viridans
entries.note: Valid name. Skin/environmental opportunist, often misID'd as viridans strep; emerging pathogen in immunocompromised/HCA hosts. Not a true commensal; most ascites isolates are contamination.
refs: {"title": "Aerococcus viridans Bacteremia: A Rare Case Report from India", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8783239/", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Bacteroides fragilis
entries.note: Valid name. Dominant anaerobe of secondary peritonitis/intra-abdominal infection; rare in true SBP (aerobic ascites). Fits potential, not verified.
refs: {"title": "Bacteroides Fragilis (StatPearls)", "url": "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK553032/", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Bacteroides ovatus
entries.note: Valid name (B. fragilis group). Gut commensal; opportunistic in polymicrobial secondary/intra-abdominal peritonitis, not SBP. Tier definition explicitly lists anaerobes here.
refs: {"title": "Resistance and Virulence Features of Bacteroides spp. Isolated from Abdominal Infections in Romanian Patients", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7696418/", "year": 2020}

entries.name: Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
entries.note: Valid name. Gut-commensal B. fragilis-group anaerobe; causes ascitic-fluid infection in secondary peritonitis (gut perforation) and PD peritonitis, rarely primary SBP. Potential confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Peritoneal Dialysis Peritonitis Caused by Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3862105/", "year": 2013}

entries.name: Candida albicans
entries.note: Most common agent of spontaneous fungal peritonitis in cirrhosis; opportunistic (HCA/antibiotic-driven, immunocompromise), high mortality, outside SBP empirical cover. Potential.
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous fungal peritonitis: Micro-organisms, management and mortality in liver cirrhosis-A systematic review", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6669191/", "year": 2019}

entries.name: Candida parapsilosis
entries.note: Leading non-albicans Candida in PD-related/fungal peritonitis; biofilm/catheter-associated, healthcare-associated ascitic infection. Valid name. Potential tier confirmed.
refs: {"title": "The Emerging Uncommon Non-Albicans Candida: Candida Parapsilosis Peritonitis in a Peritoneal Dialysis Patient", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8432431/", "year": 2021}

entries.name: Candida tropicalis
entries.note: Valid nomenclature. Non-albicans Candida documented in spontaneous fungal peritonitis of cirrhosis; opportunistic, not a bacterial SBP agent. Potential confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous fungal peritonitis: Micro-organisms, management and mortality in liver cirrhosis-A systematic review", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6669191", "year": 2019}

entries.name: Citrobacter freundii
entries.note: Valid Enterobacterales coliform; real but infrequent ascites/peritonitis agent, mostly non-classic (PD, nephrotic) settings. Not among top-cultured SBP organisms, so potential not verified.
refs: {"title": "Changes in the epidemiology and management of bacterial infections in cirrhosis", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8273641/", "year": 2021}

entries.name: Corynebacterium amycolatum
entries.note: Skin commensal/frequent contaminant in cirrhotic SBP, but documented as a true cause of PD-related peritonitis (case report), which the ascites 'potential' tier explicitly covers.
refs: {"title": "Corynebacterium amycolatum peritonitis in a patient undergoing peritoneal dialysis: case report and literature review", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11524318/", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Corynebacterium striatum
entries.note: Skin diphtheroid/common contaminant, but a documented agent of PD-associated peritonitis (device/biofilm). Opportunistic ascites pathogen in specific settings -> potential, not pure commensal.
refs: {"title": "Relapsing peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis caused by Corynebacterium striatum: a case report", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39560709/", "year": 2025}

entries.name: Cryptococcus neoformans
entries.note: The major NON-Candida cause of spontaneous FUNGAL peritonitis in cirrhosis (the systematic review found it accounted for ~53% of non-Candida SFP cases), frequently with concurrent fungemia and high mortality.
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous fungal peritonitis: Micro-organisms, management and mortality in liver cirrhosis - A systematic review", "url": "https://doi.org/10.4254/wjh.v11.i7.596", "year": 2019}

entries.name: Enterobacter cloacae
entries.note: Recognized Enterobacterales SBP agent but uncommon and predominantly nosocomial/healthcare-associated (~62% hospital-acquired), AmpC-bearing; fits potential, not verified.
refs: {"title": "Clinical characteristics and outcomes of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis caused by Enterobacter species versus Escherichia coli: a matched case-control study", "url": "https://bmcinfectdis.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12879-016-1595-y", "year": 2016}

entries.name: Enterococcus faecium
entries.note: Recognized ascitic-fluid/SBP pathogen, but E. faecium specifically clusters in nosocomial/HCA SBP and quinolone-prophylaxis patients (often VRE); best fit is potential, not community-acquired verified.
refs: {"title": "Evolving epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance in spontaneous bacterial peritonitis: a two-year observational study", "url": "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4055793/", "year": 2014}

entries.name: Fusobacterium nucleatum
entries.note: Valid name. Obligate anaerobe, oral/gut commensal; rare in secondary/polymicrobial peritoneal infection via gut spillover, not a primary SBP agent. Potential fits.
refs: {"title": "Fusobacterium nucleatum: More Than Just an Oral Anaerobe", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9386311/", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Klebsiella aerogenes
entries.note: Enterobacterales of the ESKAPE group, reclassified from Enterobacter aerogenes to Klebsiella aerogenes in 2019. An opportunistic gut-derived gram-negative bacillus with the same translocation route and AmpC/MDR concerns…
refs: {"title": "Reclassification of Enterobacter aerogenes (Hormaeche and Edwards 1960) to the genus Klebsiella as Klebsiella aerogenes comb. nov.", "url": "https://doi.org/10.1016/j.diagmicrobio.2018.12.012", "year": 2019}

entries.name: Klebsiella oxytoca
entries.note: Enteric gram-negative opportunist; Klebsiella spp. are among the most common SBP isolates and K. oxytoca specifically has documented spontaneous peritonitis episodes.
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous peritonitis due to Klebsiella oxytoca in a patient with cardiac ascites", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3189273/", "year": 1988}

entries.name: Lacticaseibacillus paracasei
entries.note: Gut commensal/probiotic (now Lacticaseibacillus paracasei); usually translocation/contaminant, but a documented SBP case (sole pathogen, neutrophilic ascites) supports rare true infection in cirrhosis -> potential, not p…
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis due to Lactobacillus paracasei in Cirrhosis", "url": "https://doi.org/10.1155/2018/5714053", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus
entries.note: Gut commensal/probiotic, but documented PD-peritonitis & cirrhosis-SBP agent via translocation; intrinsic vanco resistance. Opportunistic -> potential, not flora.
refs: {"title": "Peritonitis associated with vancomycin-resistant Lactobacillus rhamnosus in a continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis patient", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9620421/", "year": 1998}

entries.name: Micrococcus luteus
entries.note: Valid name; skin commensal/classic contaminant, but documented cause of PD-related (and relapsing, biofilm) peritonitis — fits 'potential' opportunistic ascites pathogen, not pure commensal.
refs: {"title": "Three Weeks of Treatment Induced Long-term Remission in a Patient with Micrococcus luteus-related Peritonitis", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10292988/", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Morganella morganii
entries.note: Enterobacterales gut commensal and recognized opportunistic pathogen (UTI, bacteremia, peritonitis), intrinsically AmpC-bearing.
refs: {"title": "Serratia marcescens, Morganella morganii, Klebsiella oxytoca related peritonitis attacks in a patient on automated peritoneal dialysis: A case report", "url": "https://www.revistanefrologia.com/en-serratia-marcescens-morganella-morganii-klebsiella-articulo-S2013251417301128", "year": 2017}

entries.name: Nakaseomyces glabratus
entries.note: Confirmed: 2nd-most-common Candida in spontaneous fungal peritonitis of cirrhotic ascites (6-20%) after C. albicans; azole/echinocandin resistance. Valid name now Nakaseomyces glabratus. Potential/opportunistic tier.
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous fungal peritonitis: Micro-organisms, management and mortality in liver cirrhosis-A systematic review", "url": "https://www.wjgnet.com/1948-5182/full/v11/i7/596.htm", "year": 2019}

entries.name: Parabacteroides distasonis
entries.note: Valid name (ex-Bacteroides distasonis, reclassified 2006). B. fragilis-group gut anaerobe in polymicrobial intra-abdominal/secondary peritonitis; not a classic SBP agent. Potential confirmed.
refs: {"title": "Parabacteroides distasonis: intriguing aerotolerant gut anaerobe with emerging antimicrobial resistance and pathogenic and probiotic roles in human health", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8253142/", "year": 2021}

entries.name: Peptostreptococcus anaerobius
entries.note: Valid name (LPSN). Gut-flora anaerobe; agent of polymicrobial secondary peritonitis from gut perforation/abscess, not SBP. Opportunistic = potential.
refs: {"title": "Peptostreptococcus anaerobius: Pathogenicity, identification, and antimicrobial susceptibility. Review of monobacterial infections...", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34626800/", "year": 2021}

entries.name: Phocaeicola vulgatus
entries.note: Bacteroides fragilis-group anaerobe and dominant colonic commensal. The B. fragilis group is the predominant anaerobic isolate (25-80% of cases) in secondary/polymicrobial peritonitis from bowel-derived sources.
refs: {"title": "Diagnosis and Management of Complicated Intra-abdominal Infection in Adults and Children: Guidelines by the Surgical Infection Society and the Infectious Diseases Society of America (SIS/IDSA)", "url": "https://doi.org/10.1086/649554", "year": 2010}

entries.name: Pichia kudriavzevii
entries.note: Agent of spontaneous fungal peritonitis (2nd after C. albicans, 15-25% of series); intrinsic fluconazole resistance is clinically actionable. Current name Pichia kudriavzevii.
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous fungal peritonitis: Micro-organisms, management and mortality in liver cirrhosis\u2014A systematic review", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6669191/", "year": 2019}

entries.name: Prevotella bivia
entries.note: Valid name (ex Bacteroides bivius); anaerobic GNR, genital/gut flora; role in polymicrobial secondary peritonitis, not classic SBP. Potential tier confirmed.
refs: {"title": "An unusual case of fulminant generalized peritonitis secondary to purulent salpingitis caused by Prevotella bivia - case report with literature review", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7117888/", "year": 2020}

entries.name: Prevotella melaninogenica
entries.note: Pigmented anaerobic gram-negative bacillus (oral/gut commensal) seen in polymicrobial secondary peritonitis and intra-abdominal abscess.
refs: {"title": "Diagnosis and Management of Complicated Intra-abdominal Infection in Adults and Children: Guidelines by the Surgical Infection Society and the Infectious Diseases Society of America (SIS/IDSA)", "url": "https://doi.org/10.1086/649554", "year": 2010}

entries.name: Proteus mirabilis
entries.note: Valid Enterobacterales; documented but infrequent SBP agent (~4% of cultures), not among the most-frequent (E. coli/Klebsiella). Demote verified->potential.
refs: {"title": "Novel pathomechanism for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis: disruption of cell junctions by cellular and bacterial proteases", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8862089/", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
entries.note: Valid species; minority SBP isolate (~0.7-2%), not a top community-acquired agent. Opportunistic/MDR role in nosocomial-HCA SBP fits potential, not verified.
refs: {"title": "Causative agents and outcome of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in cirrhotic patients: community-acquired versus nosocomial infections", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6533661/", "year": 2019}

entries.name: Rothia mucilaginosa
entries.note: Oral commensal, usually contaminant in ascites, but documented single-pathogen PD-associated peritonitis -> potential, not flora_commensal. Name valid (was Stomatococcus mucilaginosus).
refs: {"title": "Peritonitis from Rothia mucilaginosa in a chronic peritoneal dialysis patient", "url": "https://academic.oup.com/ckj/article/6/5/552/377207", "year": 2013}

entries.name: Serratia marcescens
entries.note: Valid name. Enterobacterales but uncommon SBP agent, skewed to nosocomial/HCA & resistant; not among top community-acquired SBP organisms. Demote verified->potential.
refs: {"title": "Epidemiological Study of Pathogens in Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis in 2017-2024 - University Hospital in South-Eastern Poland", "url": "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11123777/", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Staphylococcus aureus
entries.note: Real but infrequent SBP agent (~2-4%), concentrated in nosocomial/HCA episodes w/ notable MRSA; not a top community-acquired organism. Potential, not verified.
refs: {"title": "Predictive Factors of Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis Caused by Gram-Positive Bacteria in Patients With Cirrhosis", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4998712/", "year": 2016}

entries.name: Staphylococcus capitis
entries.note: CoNS skin commensal, usually paracentesis contaminant, but a documented opportunistic agent of PD-associated peritonitis & healthcare-assoc SBP -> potential, not pure flora.
refs: {"title": "Risk Factors and Pathogen Spectrum in Continuous Ambulatory Peritoneal Dialysis-Associated Peritonitis: A Single Center Retrospective Study", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9422442/", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Staphylococcus caprae
entries.note: Valid CoNS skin commensal; documented as sole agent of PD-related peritonitis (true infection), matching 'potential' (PD/HCA setting). Not pure contaminant.
refs: {"title": "Peritoneal Dialysis-Related Peritonitis Caused by Staphylococcus caprae: A Case Report", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12381540/", "year": 2025}

entries.name: Staphylococcus epidermidis
entries.note: Leading PD-peritonitis pathogen and HCA/catheter-related ascites opportunist; common skin contaminant in cirrhotic SBP, not a primary community-acquired SBP agent.
refs: {"title": "Coagulase Negative Staphylococcal Peritonitis in Peritoneal Dialysis Patients: Review of 232 Consecutive Cases", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2390994/", "year": 2008}

entries.name: Staphylococcus haemolyticus
entries.note: Valid CoNS; usually paracentesis skin contaminant, but a biofilm/device-associated opportunist cultured in nosocomial/HCA SBP -> potential, not pure commensal.
refs: {"title": "Epidemiological Study of Pathogens in Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis in 2017-2024 - A Preliminary Report of the University Hospital in South-Eastern Poland", "url": "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11123777/", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Staphylococcus hominis
entries.note: Valid CoNS skin commensal; usual paracentesis contaminant, but a documented opportunistic agent of PD-related/HCA peritonitis -> potential, not flora_commensal.
refs: {"title": "Coagulase Negative Staphylococcal Peritonitis in Peritoneal Dialysis Patients: Review of 232 Consecutive Cases", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2390994/", "year": 2008}

entries.name: Staphylococcus warneri
entries.note: Skin-commensal CoNS; usually paracentesis contaminant in SBP, but a documented opportunist in PD-related peritonitis (~7% of CoNS cases) -> potential, not pure commensal.
refs: {"title": "Peritoneal Dialysis-Related Peritonitis due to Coagulase-Negative Staphylococcus: A Review of 115 Cases in a Brazilian Center", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4046731/", "year": 2014}

entries.name: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia
entries.note: Valid name. MDR non-fermenter; documented but uncommon cause of SBP/intra-abdominal infection in cirrhosis, mainly healthcare-associated/antibiotic-selected. Potential, not verified.
refs: {"title": "Clinical Characteristics of Patients with Intra-Abdominal Infection Caused by Stenotrophomonas maltophilia", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12155589/", "year": 2025}

entries.name: Streptococcus constellatus
entries.note: Member of the Streptococcus anginosus (milleri) group, oral/GI commensals with a pyogenic, abscess-forming reputation in intra-abdominal infection and peritonitis. S. anginosus is already listed; its congeners S.
refs: {"title": "Intra-Abdominal Abscess and Primary Peritonitis Caused by Streptococcus anginosus", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5011413/", "year": 2016}

entries.name: Streptococcus dysgalactiae
entries.note: Beta-hemolytic group C/G streptococcus that, like the listed S. pyogenes (group A) and S. agalactiae (group B), can cause invasive infection and bacteremia/peritonitis in patients with chronic liver disease.
refs: {"title": "Bacterial infections other than spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in cirrhosis", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3365435/", "year": 2012}

entries.name: Streptococcus gordonii
entries.note: Viridans (sanguinis/mitis) group oral commensal in the same underestimated-VGS-SBP category as the other viridans streptococci already listed (sanguinis, parasanguinis, mitis).
refs: {"title": "Viridans group streptococci: an underestimated cause of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in cirrhotic patients with ascites", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16093870/", "year": 2005}

entries.name: Streptococcus intermedius
entries.note: Streptococcus anginosus/milleri group member; oral and gut commensal strongly associated with abscess formation and intra-abdominal/hepatic infection. Same rationale and tier as S.
refs: {"title": "Intra-Abdominal Abscess and Primary Peritonitis Caused by Streptococcus anginosus", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5011413/", "year": 2016}

entries.name: Streptococcus oralis
entries.note: Viridans group streptococcus (oral/GI commensal). VGS are an underestimated cause of SBP/bacterascites in cirrhotics (responsible for a large share of streptococcal SBP episodes).
refs: {"title": "Viridans group streptococci: an underestimated cause of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in cirrhotic patients with ascites", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16093870/", "year": 2005}

entries.name: Streptococcus pyogenes
entries.note: S. pyogenes (valid name) is a documented but rare cause of ascitic-fluid infection—primarily primary peritonitis in healthy hosts (often gynecologic source), <50 reported cases; streptococcal SBP is dominated by viridans…
refs: {"title": "Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis: recent guidelines and beyond", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22147550/", "year": 2012}

entries.name: Veillonella parvula
entries.note: Anaerobic gram-negative coccus and oral/GI commensal occasionally recovered in polymicrobial intra-abdominal/anaerobic infections.

entries.name: [Candida] auris
entries.note: Emerging multidrug-resistant Candida of major nosocomial concern; cirrhotics with prior antifungal/antibiotic exposure and ICU stay are exactly the at-risk SFP population.

entries.name: Aeromonas hydrophila
entries.note: Water-borne gram-negative that causes SBP in advanced cirrhosis, often seasonal (warm months) and associated with diarrhea; described as a highly fatal form of spontaneous peritonitis. Aeromonas spp.
refs: {"title": "Aeromonas spontaneous bacterial peritonitis: a highly fatal infectious disease in patients with advanced liver cirrhosis", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19369176/", "year": 2009}

entries.name: Clostridium ramosum
entries.note: Anaerobic gut commensal clostridium implicated in intra-abdominal/abdominal infections (cholecystitis, peritonitis) from bowel perforation/obstruction.
refs: {"title": "Overview of Clostridial Infections", "url": "https://www.msdmanuals.com/professional/infectious-diseases/anaerobic-bacteria/overview-of-clostridial-infections", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Kocuria rosea
entries.note: Valid name (ex-Micrococcus); skin/oral commensal & common contaminant, but documented PD-associated peritonitis & opportunistic infections fit ascites 'potential' tier.
refs: {"title": "Peritonitis attributable to Kocuria rosea in a pediatric peritoneal dialysis patient", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22991024/", "year": 2012}

entries.name: Staphylococcus cohnii
entries.note: Low-virulence skin CoNS, usually a paracentesis contaminant, but documented as true SBP agent in HCA/immunocompromised (hemodialysis+cirrhosis) cases; opportunistic, not pure commensal.
refs: {"title": "Staphylococcus cohnii infection diagnosed by metagenomic next generation sequencing in a patient on hemodialysis with cirrhotic ascites: a case report", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10556727/", "year": 2023}

lists.label: Ascites · commensal / contaminant
lists.help: Gut/skin commensals; in ascitic fluid usually skin contamination at  paracentesis or gut-translocation background rather than true infection.

entries.name: Bacillus subtilis
entries.note: Valid name. Ascitic-fluid study classes B. subtilis (with CoNS) from low-WCC samples as organism of no clinical significance—contaminant, not true SBP.
refs: {"title": "P09 Incidence of bacterascites and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) at a tertiary care teaching hospital", "url": "https://academic.oup.com/jacamr/article/7/Supplement_4/dlaf230.016/8363760", "year": 2025}

entries.name: Bifidobacterium longum
entries.note: Low-virulence gut anaerobic commensal; ascitic detection reflects translocation/contamination, not SBP. Only a single secondary-peritonitis (bowel-perforation) case report exists.
refs: {"title": "Peritonitis caused by Bifidobacterium longum: case report and literature review", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24657157/", "year": 2014}

entries.name: Corynebacterium jeikeium
entries.note: Valid name (formerly CDC group JK). Lipophilic skin commensal; opportunistic line/device pathogen in immunocompromised. No SBP role; in ascites = skin contaminant.
refs: {"title": "Complete Genome Sequence and Analysis of the Multiresistant Nosocomial Pathogen Corynebacterium jeikeium K411, a Lipid-Requiring Bacterium of the Human Skin Flora", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1151758/", "year": 2005}

entries.name: Cutibacterium acnes
entries.note: Dominant skin/sebaceous commensal, classic sterile-fluid culture contaminant; in ascites isolation usually reflects paracentesis skin contamination, not SBP. Name current (ex-Propionibacterium).
refs: {"title": "Cutibacterium acnes as an Opportunistic Pathogen: An Update of Its Virulence-Associated Factors", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7913060/", "year": 2021}

entries.name: Cutibacterium avidum
entries.note: Valid name (formerly P. avidum). Skin commensal; opportunist in implant/device/SSI, not SBP. Ascites isolates ~ paracentesis skin contamination. Agree flora_commensal.
refs: {"title": "Clinical and Biological Features of Cutibacterium (Formerly Propionibacterium) avidum, an Underrecognized Microorganism", "url": "https://journals.asm.org/doi/full/10.1128/cmr.00064-17", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Cutibacterium granulosum
entries.note: Valid name (ex-Propionibacterium granulosum, Scholz/Kilian 2016). Low-virulence skin commensal, not an SBP agent; ascitic recovery = paracentesis skin contamination.
refs: {"title": "Comparative genomic analyses of Cutibacterium granulosum provide insights into genomic diversity", "url": "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10832045/", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Lacticaseibacillus casei
entries.note: Gut/probiotic Lactobacillus; like the already-listed L. rhamnosus and L. paracasei it is normally a commensal/contaminant and only rarely an opportunist (e.g., probiotic-associated bacteremia in compromised hosts).

entries.name: Staphylococcus auricularis
entries.note: Valid CoNS (Kloos & Schleifer 1983), external-ear/skin commensal, low virulence; in ascites/SBP cultures routinely a skin contaminant from paracentesis, not a true SBP agent.
refs: {"title": "Predictive Factors of Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis Caused by Gram-Positive Bacteria in Patients With Cirrhosis", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4998712/", "year": 2016}

entries.name: Staphylococcus pasteuri
entries.note: Valid CoNS species; normal skin flora, chiefly a blood-culture contaminant. No SBP/ascites pathogen role; in ascites = paracentesis skin contamination.
refs: {"title": "Species: Staphylococcus pasteuri (LPSN)", "url": "https://lpsn.dsmz.de/species/staphylococcus-pasteuri", "year": 1993}

entries.name: Staphylococcus saccharolyticus
entries.note: Valid anaerobic CoNS skin commensal, frequent culture contaminant. Rare opportunist (bacteremia/PJI) but no SBP/ascites role; in ascitic fluid = paracentesis skin contamination.
refs: {"title": "Clinical relevance of Staphylococcus saccharolyticus detection in human samples: a retrospective cohort study", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38963607/", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Bacillus cereus
entries.note: Bacillus species (excluding B. anthracis) are environmental and transient-skin organisms counted among standard culture contaminants; a single growth from ascites usually represents contamination rather than true periton…

entries.name: Corynebacterium minutissimum
entries.note: Valid name; cutaneous coryneform (erythrasma agent). In SBP studies Corynebacterium is explicitly excluded as suspicious skin contaminant; ascitic isolation = tap contamination.
refs: {"title": "Causative agents and outcome of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in cirrhotic patients: community-acquired versus nosocomial infections", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6533661/", "year": 2019}

lists.label: Likely artifacts (removed from composition)
lists.help: Dataset-specific exclusions for recurrent assignments judged to reflect  residual host reads, reference-database problems, or clearly non-clinical  environmental signal. This is not a universal blacklist: controls and  genome-wide read coverage should be reviewed before adding taxa. Listed taxa  are removed and within-sample RA is renormalised.

entries.name: Toxoplasma gondii
entries.note: Known host/reference cross-mapping risk: human sequence embedded in T. gondii references can create large false-positive assignments. Excluded here because this dataset's recurrent/high-abundance pattern matches that failure mode; genuine toxoplasmosis still requires clinical and orthogonal confirmation.
refs: {"title": "Using populations of human and microbial genomes for organism detection in metagenomes", "url": "https://genome.cshlp.org/content/25/7/1056", "year": 2015}
{"title": "Use of the CHM13-T2T genome improves metagenomic analysis by minimizing host DNA contamination", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12542756/", "year": 2025}

entries.name: Eimeria tenella
entries.note: Chicken-specific caecal coccidian; a recurrent call in human urine/ascites is biologically discordant. Its highly repetitive genome and contamination-prone oocyst preparations make a classifier/reference artifact plausible, so this is a dataset-specific exclusion rather than a universal blacklist.
refs: {"title": "The complete genome sequence of Eimeria tenella, a common gut parasite of chickens", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8515493/", "year": 2021}
{"title": "Chromosome-level genome assembly of Eimeria tenella at the single-oocyst level", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11912684/", "year": 2025}

entries.name: Besnoitia besnoiti
entries.note: Bovine coccidian not known to infect humans naturally. Genome material has been propagated in human fibroblasts and assembly workflows explicitly removed human host reads, giving recurrent human-sample assignments a credible host/reference cross-mapping route. This remains a dataset-specific exclusion.
refs: {"title": "Besnoitia besnoiti intermediate host life-cycle stages: from morphology to gene expression", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9714946/", "year": 2022}
{"title": "EFSA assessment of animal diseases caused by Besnoitia besnoiti", "url": "https://animal-diseases.efsa.europa.eu/Besnoitia", "year": 2026}

entries.name: Puccinia striiformis
entries.note: Obligate biotrophic wheat stripe-rust fungus. Its detection here is treated as a dataset-specific non-clinical/environmental assignment; the source establishes plant ecology, not a proven human-read misclassification.
refs: {"title": "Distinct life histories impact dikaryotic genome evolution in Puccinia striiformis causing stripe rust in wheat", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7250506/", "year": 2020}

entries.name: Ascochyta rabiei
entries.note: Host-specialised fungus causing Ascochyta blight of chickpea. Its detection here is treated as a dataset-specific non-clinical/environmental assignment; the source establishes plant ecology, not a proven human-read misclassification.
refs: {"title": "Ascochyta rabiei: A threat to global chickpea production", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9366070/", "year": 2022}

lists.label: Human skin-associated bacteria (context only)
lists.help: Cross-site context only: species repeatedly recovered from healthy human skin  by culture or sequencing. Association is site-, strain- and host-dependent;  membership does not prove contamination, benignity or skin origin, and many  listed taxa are opportunistic pathogens. These taxa remain in composition views.

entries.name: Cutibacterium acnes
entries.note: Dominant, often stable resident of sebaceous skin and follicles (formerly Propionibacterium acnes); strain/context dependent and capable of acne and deep or device-associated infection.
refs: {"title": "Interference and co-existence of staphylococci and Cutibacterium acnes within the healthy human skin microbiome", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9452508/", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Cutibacterium avidum
entries.note: Minor resident of moist or occluded skin such as the axilla and groin (formerly Propionibacterium avidum); recognized surgical-site and prosthetic-joint opportunist.
refs: {"title": "Clinical and biological features of Cutibacterium avidum, an underrecognized microorganism", "url": "https://doi.org/10.1128/CMR.00064-17", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Cutibacterium granulosum
entries.note: Low-abundance cutaneous commensal (formerly Propionibacterium granulosum); rare opportunistic infections are reported.
refs: {"title": "Comparative genomic analyses of Cutibacterium granulosum provide insights into genomic diversity", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10832045/", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Staphylococcus epidermidis
entries.note: Ubiquitous, often stable healthy-skin coagulase-negative staphylococcus; also a major biofilm and device-associated opportunistic pathogen.
refs: {"title": "Integrated genomic and functional analyses of human skin-associated Staphylococcus reveal extensive inter- and intra-species diversity", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10666031/", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Staphylococcus hominis
entries.note: One of the most prevalent healthy-skin staphylococci across body sites, often enriched at moist sites; can cause catheter or bloodstream infection.
refs: {"title": "Integrated genomic and functional analyses of human skin-associated Staphylococcus reveal extensive inter- and intra-species diversity", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10666031/", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Staphylococcus capitis
entries.note: Prominent healthy-skin coagulase-negative staphylococcus with a head/sebaceous-site preference; also a neonatal and device-associated opportunist.
refs: {"title": "Integrated genomic and functional analyses of human skin-associated Staphylococcus reveal extensive inter- and intra-species diversity", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10666031/", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Staphylococcus haemolyticus
entries.note: Frequent skin coagulase-negative staphylococcus, especially at axillary and pubic moist sites; clinically important multidrug-resistant and device-associated opportunist.
refs: {"title": "Integrated genomic and functional analyses of human skin-associated Staphylococcus reveal extensive inter- and intra-species diversity", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10666031/", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Staphylococcus warneri
entries.note: Lower-abundance but widespread skin coagulase-negative staphylococcus; usually commensal, yet capable of device, bloodstream, endocardial and urinary infection.
refs: {"title": "Integrated genomic and functional analyses of human skin-associated Staphylococcus reveal extensive inter- and intra-species diversity", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10666031/", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Staphylococcus caprae
entries.note: Colonizes healthy human skin, nails and nasal mucosa; occasional opportunist, particularly in bone, joint and device infections.
refs: {"title": "Staphylococcus caprae: a skin commensal with pathogenic potential", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6314791/", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Staphylococcus auricularis
entries.note: Site-specific healthy-skin coagulase-negative staphylococcus strongly associated with the external auditory canal; rare opportunistic infection is possible.
refs: {"title": "Integrated genomic and functional analyses of human skin-associated Staphylococcus reveal extensive inter- and intra-species diversity", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10666031/", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Corynebacterium tuberculostearicum
entries.note: Predominant, widespread lipophilic Corynebacterium on healthy skin; belongs to a close species complex, so exact species calls can be reference-dependent; occasional multidrug-resistant opportunist.
refs: {"title": "Genomic characterization of the Corynebacterium tuberculostearicum species complex, a prominent member of the human skin microbiome", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10790575/", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Corynebacterium kefirresidentii
entries.note: Skin- and nares-associated member of the Corynebacterium tuberculostearicum species complex; exact assignment can be reference-dependent and should be interpreted cautiously.
refs: {"title": "Genomic characterization of the Corynebacterium tuberculostearicum species complex, a prominent member of the human skin microbiome", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10790575/", "year": 2024}

entries.name: Corynebacterium kroppenstedtii
entries.note: Lipophilic skin-associated Corynebacterium reported among healthy facial-skin taxa; also strongly associated with granulomatous mastitis.
refs: {"title": "Cultivation and characterization of the healthy human facial skin microbiome", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10683109/", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Corynebacterium striatum
entries.note: Constituent of normal skin microbiota, but an increasingly important multidrug-resistant nosocomial and device-associated opportunist.
refs: {"title": "Corynebacterium striatum: an emerging multidrug-resistant opportunistic pathogen", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36534203/", "year": 2022}

entries.name: Corynebacterium jeikeium
entries.note: Lipid-dependent member of human skin flora; clinically important multidrug-resistant opportunist in immunocompromised or device-bearing hosts.
refs: {"title": "Complete genome sequence and analysis of Corynebacterium jeikeium K411, a lipid-requiring bacterium of the human skin flora", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1151758/", "year": 2005}

entries.name: Corynebacterium amycolatum
entries.note: Typical healthy-skin corynebacterial commensal; occasionally causes infection, especially when barriers or host defenses are impaired.
refs: {"title": "Corynebacterium amycolatum: an unexpected pathogen in the ear", "url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29066761/", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Corynebacterium simulans
entries.note: Skin-associated Corynebacterium documented in healthy facial-skin surveys; species identification can be difficult and invasive infection is reported.
refs: {"title": "Cultivation and characterization of the healthy human facial skin microbiome", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10683109/", "year": 2023}

entries.name: Finegoldia magna
entries.note: Anaerobic commensal of skin and other non-sterile surfaces (formerly Peptostreptococcus magnus); also a comparatively virulent opportunist in wounds and soft tissue.
refs: {"title": "Identification of molecular mechanisms used by Finegoldia magna to penetrate and colonize human skin", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4241043/", "year": 2014}

entries.name: Lawsonella clevelandensis
entries.note: Common inhabitant of oily or sebaceous skin and nostrils, often missed by routine culture; documented cause of deep abscess and graft or device infection.
refs: {"title": "New insights into human nostril microbiome from the expanded Human Oral Microbiome Database", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6280432/", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Micrococcus luteus
entries.note: Frequent aerobic resident of healthy skin, especially dry sites; also environmental and a rare catheter-associated or immunocompromised-host opportunist.
refs: {"title": "Draft genome sequences of Micrococcus luteus strains isolated from the skin of healthy volunteers", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7303413/", "year": 2020}

entries.name: Acinetobacter johnsonii
entries.note: Recovered from skin of healthy and hospitalized people; also environmental and occasionally opportunistic.
refs: {"title": "Distribution of Acinetobacter species on human skin", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC230069/", "year": 1997}

entries.name: Acinetobacter lwoffii
entries.note: A frequent human-skin Acinetobacter in culture-based surveys; also environmental and a rare opportunist.
refs: {"title": "Distribution of Acinetobacter species on human skin", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC230069/", "year": 1997}

entries.name: Acinetobacter radioresistens
entries.note: Recognized, less frequent human-skin colonizer with strong desiccation tolerance; also environmental and occasionally opportunistic.
refs: {"title": "Distribution of Acinetobacter species on human skin", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC230069/", "year": 1997}

entries.name: Moraxella osloensis
entries.note: Skin-associated Gram-negative species isolated from healthy human skin; abundance varies by population and site, and rare invasive infection occurs.
refs: {"title": "Commensal Gram-negative skin microbiota triggers type I immunity", "url": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5773745/", "year": 2018}

entries.name: Peptoniphilus harei
entries.note: Anaerobic Gram-positive coccus of skin and mucosal microbiota; not skin-exclusive and can act as an opportunist in polymicrobial skin or soft-tissue infection.
refs: {"title": "Gram-positive anaerobic cocci \u2014 commensals and opportunistic pathogens", "url": "https://academic.oup.com/femsre/article/37/4/520/2399123", "year": 2013}
